title: Code and data for: Integrating remote sensing and natural radionuclides to assess environmental variability in a Brazilian desertification nucleus
description:
R scripts and data supporting the manuscript Integrating remote sensing and natural radionuclides to assess environmental variability in a Brazilian desertification nucleus (Silva et al., submitted to Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment).

The study compares two Caatinga (seasonally dry tropical forest) patches on Assunção Island, within the Cabrobó desertification nucleus (Pernambuco, Brazil), by combining bimonthly Landsat NDVI time series (2000–2022) analysed with BFAST and natural radionuclide activity concentrations in soil (40K, 226Ra, 228Ra and 228Th), analysed with linear mixed models and machine learning classifiers (Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine, with permutation importance and SHAP values).

The repository contains the analysis scripts, raw inputs (NDVI composites exported from Google Earth Engine, laboratory activity concentrations and plot coordinates), processed outputs, the manuscript figures and Table 1.
